title: Combination Sum II
prompt:
Given `candidates` (may contain duplicates) and a `target`, return all unique combinations summing to target. Each number may be used **at most once**.

**Example**: `candidates = [10,1,2,7,6,1,5]`, `target = 8` → `[[1,1,6],[1,2,5],[1,7],[2,6]]`.

Sort, recurse with `i + 1` (each used once), and skip duplicate siblings.
hints: Sort candidates. Track remaining target; record a copy when it hits 0.
Recurse with `i + 1` so each element is used once.
Skip duplicate siblings: `if (i > start && candidates[i] == candidates[i-1]) continue;`. Break early once `candidates[i] > remaining`.

solution.explanation: Two differences from Combination Sum I: `i + 1` (no reuse) and the duplicate-sibling skip (so `[1,7]` from the two different 1s appears once). The sorted-order `break` prunes candidates too big to fit — a free speedup.
